title: ‘It’s not the truth’: Illinois Rep. Jonathan Jackson accused of lying about the real reason he missed Pete Hegseth impeachment vote as his ‘traffic incident’ excuse is publicly challenged
content:
Illinois Democratic Rep. Jonathan Jackson is facing accusations that he misrepresented why he missed a crucial House vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after a reporter publicly challenged his explanation that a traffic incident kept him from reaching the chamber.

Pete Hegseth impeachment vote

Jackson was among 11 Democrats who missed the vote on a motion to refer eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, introduced by Republican Rep. Thomas Massie, back to committee.

The motion passed 211-204, effectively blocking the impeachment effort. Had all 11 absent Democrats voted against the motion, they could have changed the outcome.

Following the vote, Jackson blamed transportation delays for his absence.

“A traffic incident and a police-escorted bus caused a delay that resulted in the vote closing before I, along with other members, could reach the chamber. I have since entered my NO vote in the Congressional Record,” the congressman said at the time. “I remain firm in my position that Secretary Hegseth must be held accountable and impeached.”

Jonathan Jackson spotted before the vote

TMZ Washington reporter Charlie Cotton disputed Jackson’s account, claiming he personally witnessed the House representative outside the Capitol several minutes before voting ended.

Cotton alleged Jackson was recording a social media video rather than entering the chamber.

“I saw Jonathan Jackson filming a social media video about the Hegseth impeachment. And that would have been at about 5:57, 5:58 p.m. The Hegseth impeachment vote did not close until 6:05 p.m. And he was on the steps, like, that’s where the vote is. Just go inside, you’re right there. So what happened in that time, I don’t know, but the traffic jam thing, it’s not the truth — or it’s not the whole truth,” Cotton alleged.

Doubling down

TMZ did not publish photographic or video evidence showing Jackson outside the chamber during that period, but they did confront Jackson about the discrepancy in an interview on Wednesday, November 11.

“I had seen you having arrived on the steps with minutes to spare. So, I’m sorry to put you in a tricky position, but I’ve got to know: Why didn’t you vote?” Cotton asked.

Jackson acknowledged missing the vote while reiterating his explanation.

“I missed the vote — there was a traffic jam that was there. It’s inexcusable; let’s not make an excuse for it. I should have been able to make the vote; it was a procedural vote,” Jackson responded. “I stand by; I was the first member of Congress to call for Pete Hegseth to resign. I wish I could answer you in any more detail, but I support his removal.”

The controversy also reached social media, where a Community Note referencing TMZ’s reporting was attached to Jackson’s X post explaining his absence.

Other missing votes

According to ABC News, the vote was initially scheduled for 15 minutes but remained open for 29 minutes.

Other absent Democrats included former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and Representatives Haley Stevens, Laura Gillen, Steven Horsford, Julia Brownley, J. Luis Correa, Brittany Pettersen, Melanie Stansbury, Marilyn Strickland and Frederica Wilson.

title: Donald Trump blames Republican candidates for midterm losses after telling voters to put him on the ballot: ‘The people didn’t believe in the candidates,’ president says
content:
President Donald Trump has refused to accept responsibility for Republicans’ midterm election losses, according to Stephen A. Smith.

The ESPN commentator discussed his recent White House meeting with the president during a November 12 appearance on Sean Hannity‘s eponymous Fox News show.

Trump was ‘immovable’ on midterm election blame

Smith said they discussed Republicans’ midterm losses and that Trump wouldn’t budge when asked whether he bore any responsibility.

“We talked about the devastating losses in the midterms and how the GOP essentially got slaughtered,” Smith said on Hannity.

“I asked him, is he willing to point the finger at himself, and he was dogged. He was ‘no way.’ He was immovable in that regard.”

Trump had urged voters to treat the midterms as though he were on the ballot, but during their interview, which Smith shared on November 12, the president argued that he wasn’t personally on the ballot.

Trump questions Republican candidates’ appeal to voters

Trump suggested to Smith that voters were dissatisfied with Republican candidates rather than with him.

“Well, they didn’t do it. They didn’t put me on the ballot. The people didn’t believe in the candidates, perhaps,” the president said.

Smith later recounted their exchange to Hannity, saying, “He said, ‘I wasn’t on the ballot.’ I said, ‘That makes absolutely no sense, Mr. President. You said, put you on a ballot. That’s what you told the American people to do.’

“He said, ‘Well, they didn’t do it.’ I said, ‘Well, what if they did do it and that was the reason you lost.'”

Stephen A. Smith on pressing Trump over the GOP's midterm losses:

"He said, 'I wasn't on the ballot.' I said, 'That makes absolutely no sense, Mr. President. You said put you on the ballot… What if they did do it, and that was the reason you lost?'" pic.twitter.com/Qzh1WBLTer

— Furkan Gözükara (@FurkanGozukara) November 13, 2026

Smith continued, “He refused to accept that. His attitude is that the candidates were not that great. If it were him that was running, this would not have happened. That’s his mentality.”

Smith disagreed with Trump’s assessment of the midterms, arguing that voters were dissatisfied with his presidency.

“I think that he is somebody that is convinced his way is what it is. I just don’t agree with him,” Smith said.

“I think the American people made a statement against what they were seeing from him in terms of him not having his eye on the ball and coming across as a bit detached in their eyes.”

Smith addresses White House press secretary rumors

Smith told Hannity that Trump also pushed back when they discussed the impact of the Iran war and tariffs on voters and the economy.

He also dismissed speculation that Trump had offered him the role of White House press secretary.

“That was absolutely hilarious. Evidently, they don’t know about the life that I live and the kind of affluence that ESPN and Disney have blessed me with,” he said.

“I wouldn’t take that pay cut for almost anything but the presidency. That ain’t happening. Press secretary? Please.”

Smith warns Democrats about divisions within party

Smith, who has criticized both Democrats and Republicans, also warned that the Democratic Party faces challenges from its progressive wing.

“I definitely think that right now, the Democrats have a challenge on their hands because clearly there’s a lot of people out there that view the Democratic Party as a divided party,” he said.

“Now they will tell you they’re a very big tent and there’s room for everybody, but I think that the progressive left has shown you there isn’t room for everybody.

“If you’re not willing to capitulate to their desires, their wishes and their ideological beliefs 100 percent, then they got a problem with you.”

title: Rudy Giuliani warns he sees ‘certain dangers’ in J.D. Vance’s personality that make him ‘a dangerous possibility as president,’ says he’s ‘very, very nervous’ about the vice president’s handling of Iran
content:
Rudy Giuliani said J.D. Vance has a shot at the White House, but that aspects of the vice president’s personality worry him. 

During a livestream on his YouTube channel, the former New York City mayor shared his thoughts on the future of the Republican Party after its midterm losses. 

He also explained why he has some reservations about Vance, including the way he’s responded to the war in Iran. 

‘Presidential potential’

While speaking about Vance’s chances of becoming president, Giuliani said he sees potential in him. 

However, he also sees some qualities that could make him a risky choice for the country.

“I see presidential potential with you,” Giuliani said. “I also see certain dangers in your personality that make you a dangerous possibility as president.” 

Who to support

Giuliani brought up other Republicans who could be in the running, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Sen. Ted Cruz.  

“Frankly, I look at some of your colleagues very superficially so far,” he said. “Well, not Marco [Rubio] because I’ve known Marco since he was a kid, but even Ted Cruz. And I have my leanings.”

Giuliani added that it was too early to decide who he would support, but implied his endorsement would carry weight. 

“I have for some time, but I’m not stupid enough to make up my mind now. So, it might be possible I support you, and you may want it or not want it. To me, it would be important who I support.”

Vance on the Iran war 

Giuliani also questioned Vance’s take on the war in Iran. After Democrats won majorities in the House and Senate, Vance blamed the conflict for contributing to the party’s losses. 

The vice president wrote on X that Republicans had to consider how the war affected their chances in the midterms.

“The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” he said. 

“If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.” 

‘Very nervous’

Giuliani said he was most concerned about how Vance reacted to threats made against the country and its leadership.

“But it’s making me very, very nervous that a country is burning effigies of you, and your president, and your two envoys,” he continued.

“Threatening to kill them — not just episodically — but they’ve been threatening to kill them and all their predecessors for 48 years. And because we lost an election, you want to cave in.”

title: ‘We’re a threat’: Sen. John Fetterman faces first challenge to his Pennsylvania Senate seat as fellow Democrat formally announces primary campaign
content:
Pennsylvania Sen. John Fetterman is facing his first official Democratic primary challenger ahead of his 2028 reelection campaign, as Palestinian American writer and businessman Ahmed Moor launches a bid to unseat the increasingly controversial lawmaker.

Ahmed Moor running for senator

Moor, 42, formally announced his candidacy on Monday, November 9, becoming the first Democrat to challenge Fetterman, whose support for Israel and willingness to break with his party have fueled growing frustration among Democratic voters.

A democratic socialist born in Gaza who now lives in Philadelphia, Moor has never held elected office, although he recently served on the Philadelphia Democratic City Committee.

“I’m running to end the war in Iran and to promote the dignity agenda: free healthcare, free childcare, and affordable housing,” Moor wrote on X. “I’m calling for accountability for genocide, for ICE and for corruption. And finally, for the protection of our civil liberties in America.”

Moor’s campaign faced an early setback on Wednesday, November 11, when X suspended his campaign account, which had accumulated more than 33,000 followers.

“FRIENDS! It’s official! We’re a threat. They’ve suspended the campaign account,” Moor wrote.

The reason for the suspension remains unclear. His other social media accounts remain active.

Fallout from the midterm elections

Moor’s campaign comes following the midterm elections that saw Democrats reclaim control of both chambers of Congress amid growing dissatisfaction with the United States’ relationship with Israel and the unpopular U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

President Donald Trump has since suggested cutting off aid to Israel, while Vice President J.D. Vance partly blamed Republican losses on U.S.-Israel relations.

Moor, who supports withdrawing American aid from Israel, has made the conflict central to his campaign.

“I grew up in Philadelphia, but was born in Gaza, Palestine,” his campaign website states. “A few years ago my birthplace was turned to rubble in a genocide funded by our tax dollars, with the support of politicians on both sides of the aisle who can’t find money for healthcare, transit, or removing asbestos from our schools.”

John Fetterman’s support for Israel

Independent experts commissioned by the United Nations recently accused Israel of continuing genocide against Palestinians despite a Gaza ceasefire. Israel has repeatedly denied genocide allegations.

Fetterman, meanwhile, remains a staunch Israel supporter and has increasingly alienated fellow Democrats by siding with Republicans on issues including immigration and foreign policy.

Although he has not officially announced whether he will seek a second term, Fetterman told reporters this week that he welcomes a primary challenger.

The senator’s declining approval ratings and growing isolation within the Democratic Party could complicate another Senate campaign. Fetterman also faced criticism after The Wall Street Journal reported in September that he routinely avoided constituent meetings and showed little interest in his Senate responsibilities.

Switching parties?

Before the midterms, Trump publicly encouraged Fetterman to abandon Democrats and join the Republican Party.

The senator has rejected switching parties but previously suggested he would leave Democrats if they formally adopted an anti-Israel position.

“That’s my red line,” Fetterman told CNN last year. “If the Democratic Party becomes officially anti-Israel, then that’s when I would force me out.”

title: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle display a ‘certain dissonance’ during joint public appearance as the duke appears ‘closed and protective’ of his wife, expert says
content:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle seemed off during their first public appearance since Thomas Markle Sr.‘s arrest.

According to a body language expert, the couple appeared a bit out of synch during their visit to the European Parliament in the days after Meghan’s father was charged with possession of child abuse material.

Harry and Meghan display a ‘certain dissonance’ during joint public appearance

In the wake of Thomas Sr.’s scandal, Harry and Meghan appear visibly strained by the situation.

Body language expert and astrologist Inbaal Honigman claimed in an interview that there seemed to be a “certain dissonance” between the pair at the gathering.

The commentator also noted how “closed and protective” Harry seemed to be of his wife.

Harry and Meghan are displaying ‘different body language’

With the drama swirling around them, Harry and Meghan appeared to be worlds apart from each other.

“Each of them is employing rather different body language and they’re moving quite differently to one another,” Honigman said.

“When a couple is aligned, and work towards the same goals, their legs would rise and fall together, their faces would turn towards the same sights, and they’d be in step with one another. Meghan and Harry are showing almost none of that,” she pointed out.

Harry and Meghan are ‘not a demonstration for the cameras’

Although the duo seem to be a different pages, the expert can still see the adoration between them.

“Their hand-holding is warm and loving. They hold hands strongly, comfortingly, in an unmoving, clean and uniform way, which shows that this is their habit, not a demonstration for the cameras,” Honigman explained.

“It is safe to assume that they hold hands in private, too,” she added.

Harry and Meghan appeared ‘humble’ during their visit to Brussels

The appearance highlighted how deeply the arrest of Thomas Sr. has been on Harry and Meghan.

“Another thing that the pair have in common is their lowered chins. Their visit to Brussels is a humble one,” Honigman claimed.

“The couple wants to be able to make a helpful change in the world. They’re not posing. They’re paying attention,” she added.

title: ICE agent caught on video ordering ‘strike to the face’ before fellow agent punches Minnesota father as daughter pleads: ‘Why are you taking him?’
content:
An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent was caught on video ordering a “strike to the face” before another agent punched a father during an arrest outside his Robbinsdale, Minn., home.

The footage shows 45-year-old Jose Ruelas Viorato clinging to a porch support post as his daughter cries and questions why federal agents are taking him away.

The November 11 arrest, which was recorded from multiple angles, shows two immigration agents struggling to restrain Viorato before pulling him away from the porch and placing him inside a vehicle.

Viorato’s attorney has challenged the legality of his arrest, alleging that agents detained him without a warrant. But ICE has defended its officers’ actions, saying Viorato resisted arrest and physically assaulted agents.

Video shows punch during arrest

Footage of the encounter shows two ICE agents attempting to handcuff Viorato as he holds onto a support post outside his home.

His daughter can be heard pleading with the agents, saying, “He’s in the process of getting papers! Why are you taking him?” according to FOX 9.

As the agents attempt to restrain him, Viorato briefly grabs one agent’s leg. According to WCCO, one agent tells another to “strike to the face” moments before the second agent punches Viorato.

The agents eventually pull him away from the post, drag him toward a vehicle and push him into the backseat.

Attorney challenges legality of ICE arrest

FOX 9 identified Viorato as a native of Mexico. He is being held at Sherburne County jail, a facility that houses ICE detainees.

Court records reviewed by the local news outlet show that Viorato has multiple traffic violations and a petty misdemeanor trespassing offense involving private property at a campground. However, the records do not show a history of violent offenses.

His family says he has been working through the immigration system to obtain legal status and has been waiting for years.

According to WCCO, his children, Chelsea Bernal and Andres Ruelas, are U.S. citizens. The family said their father has been waiting to obtain legal status since 1999, although the outlet could not independently confirm his current standing in the immigration process.

ICE agents attempt to break a man’s arm, then punch him as his daughter watches in horror. Robbinsdale, Minnesota 11/11/26 pic.twitter.com/TG5Awlpoel

— TheSidewalkSchool (@SidewalkSchool) November 12, 2026

Viorato’s attorney, Carrie Huxford Peltier, has also challenged the circumstances of his detention.

A habeas corpus petition filed on his behalf alleges that federal agents arrested him without a warrant. According to the filing, Viorato had returned home after purchasing groceries when agents approached him.

The petition further claims that the officers did not know his identity until they checked his driver’s license. His attorney argues that they lacked sufficient grounds to believe he was unlawfully in the country. The filing also states that Viorato has no active removal order.

Police respond to 911 call

The Robbinsdale Police Department also addressed the incident after receiving an emergency call from the residence.

According to a department news release cited by FOX 9, someone called 911 at 7:13 a.m. on November 11 to report that ICE agents were taking her father.

A responding officer subsequently arrived in the area and reported that no law enforcement personnel were present. Police also attempted to return the initial call but received no answer.

The officer eventually spoke with the woman who called 911, who reportedly acknowledged that local officers could not intervene and said she did not know why she had called.

The officer cleared the scene less than two minutes after arriving, according to the department’s account.

Robbinsdale police said that their officers are trained under the city’s Separation Agreement, which outlines their protocols involving federal immigration enforcement.

ICE defends arrest

Robbinsdale City Council Member Alejandro Caceres Aranda also addressed Viorato’s arrest on social media, describing him as a father, husband and member of the local community.

In his post, Aranda said he had spent much of the day with the family as they tried to understand what had happened. He also indicated that he would share information about potential community assistance if the family requested it.

ICE has since defended the arrest, alleging that Viorato attempted to flee, threw a bird feeder at an officer and physically assaulted agents while resisting arrest.

In a statement to FOX 9, an ICE spokesperson said Viorato had been arrested during a targeted enforcement operation and would remain in custody pending removal proceedings.

“The officer relied on his training to safely control the situation and arrest him without further incident,” the spokesperson said, adding that ICE officers are trained to use “the minimum amount of force necessary to resolve dangerous situations.”

title: Republican Sen. Thom Tillis condemns Stephen Miller’s appointment as Donald Trump’s new White House chief of staff as ‘the worst of all possible choices,’ warns ‘the president needs to rethink it’
content:
Republican Sen. Thom Tillis said President Donald Trump made a big mistake by choosing Stephen Miller as the new White House chief of staff.

During an interview with CNN’s Jake Tapper, Tillis was asked what he thought of the president’s pick, which Trump announced on Truth Social.

The retiring senator called it “the worst of all possible choices” and said Trump should reconsider.

‘Worst of all possible choices’

“The worst of all possible choices,” Tillis said. “I mean, look, Jake … this past Tuesday, Republicans lost because we lost the narrative on the border, a success that the president should have been heralding, by shutting off the border, ending the open borders policies of [Joe] Biden.”

He also said Republicans lost Hispanic voters because of the administration’s immigration and homeland security policies, both of which Miller has helped oversee. 

“We lost the Hispanic vote in large part because of the mismanagement of that policy, and Homeland Security policy, which are the two majors that Stephen Miller has declared in his time in the White House.”

Can Miller work with Democrats?

Tillis went on to question how Miller’s “polarizing” reputation would help the administration work with Democrats. 

“Now we’re talking about putting one of the most partizan, polarizing figures — and not only polarizing in terms of Republicans and Democrats, but even among Republicans!” he continued. 

“How do we think somebody as divisive of a background as Stephen Miller is going to be the olive branch we need to the new Democratic majorities in Congress to get things done?”

Trump’s ‘colossal mistake’

Tillis said he had disagreed with Trump’s advisers in the past, but that Miller’s appointment was the president’s call.

“You know, I’ve criticized a lot of the president’s advisors for bad advice that I think he authorized and created some of the environment on Tuesday,” he noted. 

“But the president made this decision, and the president needs to rethink it. It is a colossal mistake, and the last thing we need 72 hours after the [expletive] whooping we got on Tuesday.” 

‘Not in Kansas anymore’

Tillis’ comments came after a rough midterm election for Republicans. Democrats won the House after flipping more than three dozen seats held by Republicans. 

The senator also warned that the administration would have to get used to working with a Democratic majority starting in January.

“They’re not in Kansas anymore,” he said, adding, “They’re going to be in a very different world starting in January, and they need to govern that way or we’re going to see disruptions and positioning that the Democrats will use against us in ’28.”

title: Prince William comes around on Kate Middleton’s unusual hobby: ‘It’s slightly to the point where William is like, you’re crazy,’ she says
content:
Prince William seems to understand one of Kate Middleton‘s favorite hobbies.

After the Princess of Wales revealed she loves swimming in extremely cold water, her husband seems to be coming around to her odd pastime.

William comes around on Kate’s unusual hobby

During an appearance on Mike Tindall‘s “The Good, the Bad and the Rugby” podcast, Kate opened up about her favorite activity.

“Personally, I love swimming. Cold swimming, the colder [the water], the better. I absolutely love it,” she revealed.

“It’s slightly to the point where William is like, ‘You’re crazy.’ It’s dark, and it’s raining, and I seek out the cold water,'” the mother of three added.

William reveals swimming is one of his ‘favorite things’

In the magazine that William co-edited, he made a list of his “favorite things.” One of them happened to be swimming.

“I’d love us to have rivers that are clean enough for all of us to swim in,” he wrote in the article.

“There’s something about the sound of running water that I find impossible to resist,” the future king of England continued. “If I come across a beautiful stretch of river on a walk, I‘m always tempted to jump in for a quick dip in the cold water, so it pays to be prepared.”

William and Kate are ‘the best of friends’ 

Through it all, the couple have continued to keep their relationship strong.

“There is no doubt that Kate has always been his No. 1 supporter,” former butler Grand Harrold told OLBG.

“She is by his side in everything he does, so I am not surprised she has taken part in the interview,” he noted of Kate’s feature for the publication William co-edited. “She would be aware that this is a big deal for William and she would also want it to be a success. I have always said that the two of them are the best of friends and in hand the best work team.”

Kate opens up about her recovery from cancer

Upon participating in the interview, the former Duchess of Cambridge got candid about overcoming cancer.

“I was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear,” Kate explained.

“There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time. This is the same in nature,” she noted.

title: Man Arrested for Leaving Baby in Car While Gambling at Casino for 2 Hours
content:
A Florida man was arrested after he allegedly left a baby in a car for two hours while he gambled inside of a casino.

Gregory Foster has been charged with child neglect following the incident, which took place on Wednesday, November 11, according to Broward County court records viewed by Us.

Foster, 28, was taken into custody at the Broward County Sheriff’s Office’s main jail on $2,500 bond.

Authorities learned of the incident when a Seminole Police Department officer was called to the Seminole Classic Casino in Hollywood, Florida, on Wednesday around 11 a.m., according to an arrest report viewed by Law & Crime. Upon their arrival, the security personnel at the casino directed the officer to a black BMW in the parking lot.

Florida Dad Arrested After Letting Son, 4, Wander Around Busy Road

The officer noted that the vehicle did not have a driver inside, but they did find that a baby had been “left in the car.” The child was found in a car seat in the middle of the back seat, and the officer noted that the child was not safely buckled in.

The security personnel said that the BMW had been there for “over an hour” by the time the police officer arrived.

Once the officer determined that the child was not moving, they forced their way inside and found that the child “appeared to be sleeping.”

Security at the casino was able to determine that Foster owned the vehicle, and they got in touch with him to discuss the incident. Authorities said that Foster was later found inside the casino “playing at a table.”

While speaking to authorities, Foster reportedly explained that he “only left the infant in the car for 45 minutes.” However, his statement was debunked when security staff said he had been gambling inside of the casino for about two hours.

Foster was then arrested at the scene and taken into custody.

Mom, 2 Friends Arrested After Allegedly Leaving Baby in Car to Go to Bars

The court document did not identify how Foster and the child are related, and the child’s age has also not yet been revealed. It is not currently clear who has custody of the child after Foster was arrested or if the baby suffered any health problems as a result of being left in the car.

It’s not known whether Foster has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following his arrest. The Seminole Police Department did not immediately respond to Us’ request for comment regarding updates in the case.

Justin Hartley's 'Tracker' Is Relocating After Cast Exits: Change Explained

The hit CBS series, which premiered in February 2024, introduced fans to survivalist Colter, who travels the country to help solve various missing persons cases. “I’m proud of what we built in Vancouver. content:
Avril Lavigne welcomed her own little Sk8er Girl with the birth of her first baby.

“Our Mini F***ing Princess has arrived 🎀👑🍼🩷,” Lavigne, 42, revealed in a Friday, November 13, Instagram post, borrowing lyrics from her 2007 hit “Girlfriend.”

The “I’m With You” singer shared a carousel of photos celebrating her daughter’s arrival, including a shot of herself cradling the little one close to her chest. The baby is already showing off a fun sense of style in a leopard print onesie and matching headband.

It is not immediately clear who the father of the baby is, though Lavigne included photos of both of them holding their daughter’s hand. A third image features three sets of Vans sneakers on a skateboard — sized for mom, dad and baby.

View this post on Instagram

Us has reached out to Lavigne’s spokesperson for comment.

Lavigne has addressed the possibility of becoming a mom throughout her career. In 2008, the Canadian singer-songwriter downplayed the likelihood of having kids with then-husband Deryck Whibley anytime soon.

“Oh God! I don’t want to have kids for like 10 years,” she told OK! at the time. “I still have a lot to do. I don’t even know if I could handle a dog right now. I’m so not ready. Someday I’ll be a mom, but not until I’m in my 30s.”

Lavigne and Whibley’s marriage ended in 2010, and she was later wed to Nickelback frontman Chad Kroeger from 2013 to 2015.

The subject of motherhood came up again in a 2014 interview with the Toronto Sun, as Lavigne stressed that her career was still her top priority.

“I’m really focused on my career at the moment,” she told the outlet. “Down the road, I would love to be a mom, just not right now.”

Looking Back at Avril Lavigne and Brody Jenner’s Wild 2-Year Romance

In recent years, Lavigne has had a relationship with billionaire heir Phillip Sarofim from 2018 to 2019. She announced her engagement to singer and rapper Mod Sun in April 2022, though they eventually split before ever tying the knot.

“Avril and Mod Sun have been on and off for the past two months, but are no longer together as a couple,” a source exclusively told Us in February 2023.

A separate insider revealed to Us in March 2023 that Lavigne and Mod Son (real name Derek Ryan Smith) “got to know each other on a deeper level and found out it didn’t work out.”

Lavigne dodged questions about whether she was dating Tyga during a 2024 “Call Her Daddy” podcast interview, though she did open about what she expected from a partner.

“I think the most important thing is finding someone that you’re compatible with, because you could be two different great people. But if you’re not compatible, you’re not going to get along,” the singer noted. “It all just sounds cliche. Someone that is trustworthy, because if you don’t have that, you’re just never going to feel grounded in the relationship, and you’re going to be spinning. So that’s just not healthy.”

title: 3-Year-Old Told Babysitter 'Mama Cut Papa' After Mom Allegedly Killed BF
content:
A babysitter had been watching a Florida woman’s two children when the mother’s 3-year-old daughter started crying and said, “Mama cut papa,” court documents state.

The girl’s statement came the same day Orlando police discovered a man’s body in a trash bag between a dumpster and a trash compactor at the Pacifico Apartments in the city on Tuesday, November 9, according to court documents.

The child’s mother, Isidra Bautista Hernandez, is accused of killing her boyfriend inside their shared apartment at the complex two days earlier, on Saturday, November 7, and disposing of his body.

Hernandez, 36, was arrested on a second-degree murder charge in connection with the man’s death on Wednesday, November 11, Us previously reported.

Woman Killed Sleeping Boyfriend, Dismembered Body Before Burying Him in Yard

An arrest affidavit obtained by Us reveals more details about the man’s killing, identifying him as Eugenio Martinez.

On Monday, two maintenance workers initially found a heavy black garbage bag “covered in flies” with what they suspected were human remains inside near the dumpster area of the Pacifico Apartments, resulting in a 911 call, according to the affidavit.

Orlando police arrived and initially saw a man’s arm, which was wrapped in a blue sheet, inside the bag, the affidavit states.

The man identified as Martinez, 32, “was tied with an orange extension cord and wrapped in 3 black trash bags and a dark blue laundry bag,” an officer wrote in the affidavit.

An autopsy revealed he had “laceration to his neck as well as puncture wounds on his left side, lacerations on his left palm, and lacerations on the left side of his face,” the affidavit states.

Detectives searched the trash compactor that was near Martinez’s body and found several items with suspected blood, including a black sandal, a piece of mail, a broken knife, towels and blankets, according to police.

The investigation led officers to execute a search warrant at Hernandez’s apartment, where suspected blood was found throughout the residence, which appeared to have been recently cleaned, the affidavit states.

While there, a 21-year-old woman approached detectives and revealed her mother had been babysitting Hernandez’s two children — a 3-year-old daughter and a 1-year-old son — since Saturday, when the alleged killing occurred.

She said on Monday, the girl cried out saying, “‘Mama cut papa’ and made hand gestures mimicking a slicing motion along her arms, stomach, and neck,” the affidavit states.

Tennessee Man Accused of Killing His Son, 3, Hiding Body in a Suitcase

Hernandez’s daughter also mentioned “blood” and “trash” to the babysitter, according to the filing.

Hernandez, who had bruising on her arm, was detained and told officers she had been involved in a physical altercation with Martinez, whom she described as her husband but noted they’re not legally married, on Saturday, the affidavit states. She accused him of choking her while holding a long knife.

At some point, she said she took the knife from him and demonstrated a “slashing motion,” according to the filing.

“Hernandez advised that she did not contact law enforcement due to fear; however, she later placed two calls to 911 in hopes that someone would find the decedent at the dumpster,” the affidavit states.

She allegedly also admitted to placing Martinez’s body in trash bags and leaving it near the dumpster.

“Statements made by the couple’s young child referencing her mother cutting someone, along with the subsequent bruising on Hernandez’s arm, provide additional context surrounding the events preceding the decedent’s death,” the officer wrote in the affidavit.

Hernandez’s public defender didn’t immediately return a request for comment from Us on Friday, November 13.

Hernandez is due in court for a hearing set for November 17, records show.

title: Janelle James on Why ‘Abbott’ Fans May Be ‘Shocked’ at Her Netflix Special
content:
Janelle James is showing Abbott Elementary fans a different side of her comedic chops with her new Netflix special.

These are people who are coming to see the character on Abbott Elementary, and I am truly just trying to introduce myself as myself, so some people will probably be shocked because they won’t do any investigation into my stand-up career. But that also, again, is not my problem. I’m just for my people,” James, 47, exclusively told Us about Janelle James: How Romantic, which made its streaming debut on Tuesday, November 10.

The Emmy-nominated actress has been doing stand-up for over a decade, and no topic is off-limits.

“I’ve been pretty brave since I’ve started. I’ve always wanted to do taboo subjects. That’s what my mind is. I just have a dark sense of humor. I think about melancholy things. I’m a classic, sad clown. I’m thinking about sad things all the time,” she said.

James admitted that her performance, however, is “different” than when she first started in comedy.

“I think I’m more joyous in my performance now than I used to be. I’m less sad, or at least outwardly, and I’m just a more confident performer now,” she shared.

In her first-ever hour-long Netflix special, James cleverly tackles hot-button topics like body counts, bank accounts and why women should wrestle men. Her unfiltered jokes come from a woman’s point of view, and she’s ready for any male critics who might take issue.

“In this day and age, there’s always concerns, but you can’t really let them stop you from moving. So obviously, if I was so concerned, I just would not do such a female-friendly set. People are going to have things to say, regardless. I have to not ready myself for that, but just be aware of that,” James explained.
The comedian said she’s “proud” and “confident” about the special.

“[I] can’t please everybody. And I feel like any men who would have bad feedback, they just don’t get it,” she told Us.

Abbott Elementary's Sheryl Lee Ralph: How Quinta Swayed Me to Play Barbara

After 15 years in comedy, James knows her worth — and shared that earning the respect of her male peers has been just as meaningful as her success on Abbott Elementary.

“I know that I’m funny. I know I have the respect of my peers. That’s really hard. My peers are men. I have male respect in the comedy space. That’s a big deal. … then there’s all this work on Abbott and doing well at that, and just really being ready to do stand-up again. I really just had the urge,” she said.

James began her comedy career in 2009 and landed the opening act of Chris Rock‘s 2017 Total Blackout tour. She then started writing and voice acting for comedy shows like Central Park before appearing as a featured comic on Netflix’s The Standups in 2021.

James gained worldwide fame for her role as the quick-witted principal in ABC’s Abbott Elementary alongside Quinta Brunson, Tyler James Williams, Lisa Ann Walter and Sheryl Lee Ralph.

title: D.C. Gym Mass Shooter Identified as Doctor in Condo Association Lawsuit
content:
Authorities revealed that the gunman who killed one person and injured four others in a mass shooting near a gym in Washington, D.C., has been identified as Dr. Matt Lambert.

The incident took place on the morning of Thursday, November 12, when Lambert, 55, shot five people in the city’s Logan Circle neighborhood. The shootings began at the VIDA gym, and Lambert later fled to an apartment building located above the gym.

Metropolitan Police Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll said during a press conference on Thursday that Lambert barricaded himself inside an apartment on the seventh floor of the building before he died by suicide.

Carroll explained that Lambert had been involved in a dispute with his homeowner’s association at the time of the mass shooting.

Everything to Know About the White House Correspondents’ Dinner Shooting

Lambert — who was a licensed emergency medicine doctor and recently worked as a healthcare consultant — had previously filed a lawsuit against the condominium association, according to NBC Washington.

He reportedly claimed in the lawsuit that his apartment had mold and moisture issues after a contractor worked on the building.

The building manager, James Stuart, was killed in the shootings. One other person was critically injured, while three people suffered non-life-threatening injuries.

“We do know that the victim that was killed inside the VIDA was the building manager for that location. So, we do know that there has been an ongoing dispute between the suspect in this case and the building, condo, homeowners association, management regarding maintenance issues — mold and the like — that there was a civil case that he filed against them. So, we believe that it’s related to that,” Carroll said.

Lambert purchased the 1,200-square-foot penthouse in the building for $1.095 million in 2016. Five years later, he tried to sell the home for $1.275 million, according to online listings.

Joel Braithwaite, Lambert’s attorney, weighed in on the tragedy, saying, “I don’t want the story to be that litigation led to this result. Litigation is supposed to prevent these results by having people litigate in court and not have that spill into the streets.”

Lambert filed the lawsuit in 2025, claiming that he began to notice mold, moisture and water problems in the apartment in 2024. He alleged that the damage cost him over $100,000, and he sued for negligence, breach of fiduciary duty and nuisance. Additionally, Lambert asked for a jury trial.

The litigation was ongoing, and a mediation was scheduled to take place in March 2027.

Braithwaite explained that Lambert had several residences, though his D.C. apartment was his “prized possession.”

“One of the issues for us was that Matt was treated differently than a lot of other people in the units, and that was the source of some consternation for us … and that’s what resulted in litigation, because to his mind, only his complaints were not heard and addressed by the condo association,” Braithwaite said.

Braithwaite added that he was surprised by the shooting and noted that Lambert had been in “great spirits” prior to the tragedy.

title: University of Louisiana Football Player Carted Off the Field in Scary Scene
content:
University of Louisiana at Lafayette linebacker Ashley Williams was carted off the field after a scary hit in a game against the University of Louisiana at Monroe on Thursday, November 12. 

During the second quarter, Williams laid motionless on the field at UL Monroe’s St. Francis Stadium after attempting a tackle and colliding with teammate Brent Gordon Jr. 

Williams was placed on a backboard and in a neck brace as he made his way to a waiting ambulance. Players from both teams took knees on the field, with many of them gathering to pray. 

While he was being carted off, Williams managed to hold up a “UL” hand gesture for fans. He was taken to nearby St. Francis Medical Center, roughly a 10 minute drive from the stadium. 

Fernando Mendoza Shares Emotional Message to Kirk Cousins' Family After Trade

According to the ESPN2 broadcast, Williams was alert, moving his extremities, answering questions and watching the game from his hospital room. The Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns went on to defeat UL Monroe 42-21, improving to 7-3 on the season. 

Williams took to social media on Friday, November 13, reposting well-wishes via his Instagram Story. 

Ragin’ Cajuns head coach Michael Desormeaux addressed the injury after the game.

“That’s like the worst, man.” Desormeaux said. “You know, when you get out there and a player’s completely unconscious and your mind just goes to the worst things possible.”

The coach added, “By the time Ashley left, he was conscious. He was talking, he was moving. I think it was just out of a lot of precaution. I think anytime something like that happens where it’s a head shot and they’re unconscious, I think it’s the right way to do it. You know, make sure that you do it out of abundance of caution.”

A redshirt junior from Zachary, Louisiana, Williams has started every game for the Cajuns this season. Going into the game, he had earned 21 total tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks and two quarterback hurries.

In the wake of Williams’ injury, many Ragin’ Cajuns fans expressed their concerns on social media. 

“Prayers up for Ashley Williams,” one supporter wrote via X. “As passionate as we get about performance, what a quick but sickening reminder that it really doesn’t mean much in the big scheme of things.”

Another wrote, “Goodness. I absolutely hate when a player has to be carted off the field. Prayers up for Ashley Williams of Louisiana Ragin Cajuns. 🙏 🏈.”

The Cajuns return to action when they host Coastal Carolina on Saturday, November 21. Williams’ potential availability for that game has not been announced.

title: The King is Back: ‘Godzilla: Minus Zero’ Spoiler-Free Review – ScreenHub Entertainment
content:
Note: I’m going to be as spoiler-free as possible for this review. Nothing that’s not revealed in the trailers. If it sounds vague and full of holes, this is for you!

Godzilla: Minus One was a surprise hit, both for fans and Toho. It took the familiar Godzilla story and rebooted it for modern audiences. Unlike the Monsterverse going on at Warner, Minus One prioritized drama and character; these people just so happen to live in a world where Godzilla exists. So it’s not so surprising that a sequel has come about: Japan’s first feature film shot for IMAX, and thanks to the success of its predecessor, now has a wide release. So, does lightning strike twice for the franchise, or does Godzilla: Minus Zero suffer from sequelitis? Let’s find out.

Two years have passed since the events of Minus One, and Japan is still coming to grips with both emerging from the ashes of WWII and the carnage laid waste by Godzilla, seemingly defeated at the end of the last movie. But something happens that unleashes a catastrophic danger on the people of Japan and questions emerge about what to do next that’s best for the country and its people. Vague, I know, but it’s for the best.

A lot of the cast from the original film return. Ryunosuke Kamiki is front and center as Kōichi Shikishima, the pilot from the last film. He’s found happiness at long last, having married Noriko (Minami Hamabe) and accepted the role as father to the orphan Akiko, the orphaned child they both took in. Shikishima was plagued by survivor’s guilt in the first film, but has a new lease on life, which makes this new tragedy that much more impactful for him: he has something to lose now.

Other characters, such as Akitsu, the captain of the Shinsei Maru and Mizushima, his crewmate, have significantly reduced roles this time around. This is because the movie diverts a lot of screen time towards Kenji Noda (Hidetaka Yoshioka), the brilliant scientist turned director of the Large-Scale Disaster Response Bureau. Noda finds himself in a situation where the greater moral good is bogged down by what’s easy, and his arc more than a couple of times reminded me of Oppenheimer. A brilliant mind who has been put into a situation where he has become death, destroyer of worlds. Reinforcing this theme is the new character Kanji Murakami (Min Tanaka), a biologist and survivor of Hiroshima. Whereas Minus One delved into themes of life and death, Minus Zero taps into the moral grey zone of power, destruction, and retribution. There’s a fantastic, and horrifying, sequence revolving around Murakami that may just be the highlight of the movie that very much taps into the fears of atomic warfare.

It doesn’t always hit the same highs as Minus One did, that said. It does take a bit of time for the characterization and themes to really get going, and some plot points get resolved far too quickly. The depiction of the US characters also felt very cartoony. But Minus Zero is still poignant and even touching, with a lot of heart and questions to pose to the audience. So if you liked your Godzilla movie with a lot of characters you actually care about, Minus Zero continues that.

But what of the monster mayhem? There isn’t as much as you might think there would be, but what there is, is great. Let’s just say the movie wastes no time getting into it. The film really dives into that sense of scale, and that’s only bolstered by the IMAX presentation. Some of the VFX for trivial things, like birds or green-screen backgrounds while characters are on a motorcycle are jarringly rough, but rest assured, it delivers when it matters most. One sequence involving planes in the first half of the movie, was a particular highlight for me. Where the film doesn’t miss a beat though is both the score and the sound effects. Chef’s kiss. When that iconic Godzilla theme kicks in, you know you’re in for a treat.

Godzilla: Minus Zero is definitely bigger, not per se better, but still a great movie nonetheless. It keeps the story focused on its compelling characters and themes, while having them exist in these larger-than-life moments. Here’s hoping for one more Minus film to close out this story!

title: A Familiar Yet Compelling Crime Drama: ‘Paper Tiger’ Spoiler-Free Review – ScreenHub Entertainment
content:
Paper Tiger had its premiere earlier this year at the Cannes Film Festival, where it competed for the coveted Palme d’Or. A crime epic, it seeks to capture the feel and tension found in so many iconic crime films. But does it stick the landing? Let’s find out.

The film stars Miles Teller as Irwin Pearl, an engineer who ends up teaming up with his brother Gary (Adam Driver), a former NYPD officer, in establishing a lucrative side business on the docks. Of course,  nothing goes to plan, and the family quickly find themselves on the wrong side of the Russian mafia. With his wife, Ester (Scarlet Johansson) and their two sons in danger, Irwin and Gary have to find a way to keep the family safe and keep the mob off their backs.

Paper Tigers is a solid crime thriller that’s well acted and well directed. Its main roadblock is that it doesn’t really feel like it’s breaking too far from the mould, which can result in some predictability. I’ve seen variations of this film before, about a family who has gotten in way too over their head with the criminal underworld, whether intentionally or not.

Paper Tigers does at least shine, that said, especially in the acting department. Teller and Driver do great work as brothers who find their bond tested as the threat of harm and violence becomes their new reality. But it’s Johansson who excels as Ester, a frightened mother of two teenage boys. She’s rightfully scared to death, and the unexpected proximity to danger coming from her unassuming husband only makes the situation that much more baffling. Irwin isn’t a bad guy; he has no connections to crime, so the Russian mob showing up in their lives was likely the last thing on her mind.

The film also excels at bringing 1980s Queens, New York, to life. The film feels run-down, dirty, and lived-in, from the suburban home that the Pearl family lives in to the busy streets in town. In fact, both the aesthetic and criminal elements reminded me in part of Grand Theft Auto IV and Niko’s early interactions with the Russian mob in that universe’s equivalent of Brooklyn and Queens.

In the end, Paper Tiger joins a lot of movies this year that can be labelled as good, but maybe not great. It’s worth a watch if you’re into crime dramas and want one with some top-notch acting, but I don’t think you’ll be wowed by much else due to the familiarity of the narrative beats and tropes.

title: Is ‘Wildwood’ Safe For Kids? A Parent’s Spoiler-Free Review – ScreenHub Entertainment
content:
The film Wildwood has been causing a bit of a stir online, and not just because of the stunning visuals and groundbreaking multimedia artistry. Rather, it’s because a segment of parents decided to disregard the PG13 rating and take their children to see this stop-motion spectacle, not expecting some of the darker themes in the film. I was one of those parents, and I’d like to explain exactly why I am extremely happy that I took my son to see Wildwood.

Editor’s Note: The author has attempted to avoid spoilers, but does include some vague descriptions of events in the film.

The Plot

A young woman named Prue discovers a world of magic and fantasy hidden just outside the city limits of Portland, Oregon. Prue and her reluctant friend Curtis will face extreme danger, thrilling adventure, and the scourge of municipal bureaucracy in their quest to save her baby brother from a powerful sorceress driven mad by grief.

The Rating

Wildwood earned a PG-13 rating from the MPAA, and I understand why. One of the opening scenes in the film deals with suicide in a very fantastical way and, while not exactly graphic, it is definitely not subtle. Later in the story, there are some large-scale battles that display equally large-scale violence.

Though the PG-13 rating is warranted, that shouldn’t be the only thing to consider when deciding whether or not to take your child to see it. It’s true that the MPAA rating can be a valuable tool. However, sometimes it is exactly because of those “adult” themes that you should watch these movies with your children.

Can Kids Handle It?

One of the most important lessons that a parent can learn is that every child is different. So, when considering if your child can handle any film, regardless of rating or subject, it is your responsibility to judge whether your child has the ability to understand what they will see on screen.

For any parents who are unsure about Wildwood, I wrote a detailed description of ways to assess your child’s tolerance and prepare them for possible mature subjects when the film Beatlejuice Beatlejuice came out. Among other things, I evaluated my son’s ability to separate fiction from reality, explained what he could expect, and made sure he had snacks to mentally ground him.

Start the Conversation

The fact that the film Wildwood contains some delicate subjects, but is still packaged in such an accessible medium, gives parents a unique opportunity. In a 2016 interview with USA Today, Wildwood director Travis Knight said: “We respect that children are smart, sophisticated and can handle things that adults typically don’t think they can.” Despite what many think, this holds true even for subjects such as depression, grief, and suicide.

These subjects are not exclusive to adults, and stories like Wildwood give parents the opportunity to introduce these harsh concepts in a safe setting. More often than not, it is the parents who aren’t ready to talk about these subjects with their children, but it can be extremely important to try before they are confronted with them in the real world.

The temptation to protect our children from anything that might disturb them is a strong one. We always want to do what’s best for them, but sometimes what’s best for them is uncomfortable for us. We must be able to speak with our kids about difficult realities to prepare them for life. In this regard, I believe Laika Studios has done parents a great service in Wildwood.

title: ‘Wildwood’ is a Must-See – ScreenHub Entertainment
content:
More than a dozen times over the course of watching Wildwood, the latest film from Laika Studios, I caught myself thinking, “How the hell did they even make this movie?” It’s been a long time since I’ve been utterly transported by a movie, both in terms of imagination, spectacle, and craft, and yet Wildwood did just that. I didn’t bury the lede here: Wildwood is a must-see cinematic event.

Directed by Travis Knight and written by Chris Butler (both responsible for Kubo and the Two Strings), Wildwood follows a teenage girl from Portland named Prue, who, against the wishes of her parents, brings her infant brother outdoors for some fun in town despite the express instructions not to do so. Of course, she should have listened to her parents, as magical forces from beyond the Impassable Wilderness abduct her brother and bring him into the forest, a place where no one from the outside world can get in due to an impassable network of vines and trees. Yet Prue is somehow able to breach the barrier, and with the help of Curtis, a shy, dorky classmate of hers, they venture into the magical realm beyond the trees.

Much like Kubo and Coraline, Wildwood is a stop-motion animated film. Unlike those films, I forgot constantly throughout the film that it was a stop-motion animated film. The animation and attention to detail are so smooth and lifelike, removing that traditional jankiness that’s associated with the medium. Characters are lifelike and expressive, reacting to events with subtle ticks and reactions, even tearing up (this is stop-motion, don’t forget, no CG like Pixar), so little details like that really stand out. I would recommend watching this behind the scenes to fully understand the magic.

From an art/production standpoint, I must say I really love the look and feel of this movie. There are stylistic elements from the medieval period, the 18th or 19th century, and early 20th century here, creating this unique hodgepodge of costumes and architectural designs. The world is inhabited by both humans and anthropomorphic animals, most notably the coyotes, who serve the Dowager Countess Alexandra, the film’s primary antagonist. Voiced by Carey Mulligan, the Countess could’ve easily been a one-dimensional villain hellbent on just doing villainous things, but Wildwood fleshes out her backstory with tragic detail. Wildwood succeeds not only with its art and visuals, but by having a complex and layered story on top of it.

As a note: this may be an animated movie, but I would advise against bringing young children. Wildwood is a dark film, with some thematic elements that may scare younger kids. The movie opens, and you’re instantly left traumatized. There’s some frightening images too, and it doesn’t shy away from violence. There’s some humour to help lift the mood, but it never compromises the drama in any way, thankfully. But I would not call this a “light” movie at all. But kids (and parents) who are open to exploring these themes and elements have a great outlet here. As always, it’s up to the parents to gauge what is safe. Just don’t go into this one expecting a family-friendly experience the whole way. This is very much a PG-13 movie in the end.

If I did have a criticism of the film, it would be that it does resolve things fairly quickly by the end. I would’ve liked to have a bit more rumination on what happened and why. The film elects to just wrap itself up, but considering everything we just went through, I think a bit of time for Prue and Curtis to reflect with the allies they made along the way and the weight of what just happened.

As Prue and Curtis explore and learn about the world they’re now inhabiting, they discover kingdoms, magical beings, talking animals, and see vast armies clash. The scope of this movie, more than once, reminded me of The Lord of the Rings, by way of Redwall and a dash of Princess Mononoke. It’s incredibly imaginative, and knowing that so much of this movie was made by hand is fascinating and only increases that sense of awe.

Wildwood is one of those films that utterly transports you. It’s a film that was clearly made by a team of passionate artists who poured years of their lives into making this film. I would strongly encourage you to not only watch it, but to go out and support it. In an age where so many films feel soulless and bland, Wildwood is anything but.
